o1.biggest_strength: Names the leak (Essentials 8+), the hidden retention lever (yearly billing), and ships a concrete plan with a test and stop rules; the customer email is dead-on brand voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The revenue math is hand-wavy and internally inconsistent ($23,900 MRR lost vs the ~$24,700 the data implies; a '$64 typical bill' next to a $99 price with no explicit migration value case; yearly ROI framed in a confusing per-channel way).
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie every number back to the exact data rows, show the churn-savings arithmetic in the same units throughout, and quantify the Agency value gap for a switcher (what they get for +$35) in one sentence an owner can repeat.

o2.biggest_strength: Cleaner, more transparent math with a stated base case and an explicit breakeven ('loses money if more than 1 in 3 Team 8+ move down'); pricing anchored to today's real per-channel bill, which makes the switch a no-brainer for the target.
o2.biggest_mistake: Underweights the yearly-billing lever the data screams about — it's a one-line 'also offer yearly' rather than a first-class move with its own math and test, despite 0.9% vs 4.0% churn.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Promote yearly billing to a co-equal recommendation with its own revenue/churn math and a test, and show the downside-case recovery path so the owner sees how a -$20k month gets corrected.

reason: Both are usable, but Output 2's numbers are cleaner and its breakeven framing gives me a single number to watch, while Output 1 — despite spotting the yearly-billing win — muddles its own revenue math and leaves me less sure of the figure I'd quote to my board.
